about.title: Monterey Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey's economy leans heavily on hospitality, fishing, agriculture, and tourism-related trades, and each of these industries carries its own injury risks, from wet kitchen floors near Fisherman's Wharf to equipment hazards on farms off Rt 68. When a workplace injury happens, most employees in California are covered by workers' compensation, which pays medical care and partial wages regardless of fault but generally blocks a lawsuit against the employer. That said, Monterey workers are often exposed to hazards created by outside contractors, property owners, or equipment manufacturers who don't share that legal shield. LawProactive is a free service that helps injured workers get connected with an independent attorney who can look at whether a third party's negligence contributed to the injury, separate from any workers' comp claim already filed. We don't charge for the connection, and we don't guarantee any result. The goal is simply to help you find someone who can explain your options clearly.

whyChoose.title: Why Monterey Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding the Third-Party Path
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker may still be liable. An attorney can help determine whether your situation involves someone outside the workers' comp system.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. Knowing this protection exists can make it easier to report what happened without fear.

items.title: Awareness of Reporting and Filing Deadlines
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally need to be reported to the employer within 30 days, and any separate third-party injury claim carries its own two-year deadline. Missing either window can limit your options, so timing matters.

items.question: I already filed a workers' comp claim in Monterey County — can I still talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Yes, filing a workers' comp claim doesn't rule out a separate claim against a negligent third party, such as a property owner or contractor not employed by your company. An independent attorney can review your situation to see if that applies. LawProactive can help connect you with one at no cost.

items.question: What if my injury happened while delivering goods along Lighthouse Avenue or Fremont Street?
items.answer: If you were injured in a vehicle collision while working, and another driver was at fault, that may open a claim separate from workers' comp. These situations often involve both systems working together, so it helps to have someone look at the specifics. There's no cost to get connected and ask.

items.question: How long do I have to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: Generally, you should report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days to preserve your workers' comp rights. If a third party contributed to the injury, that separate claim typically carries a two-year deadline. Because these timelines differ, it's worth getting guidance sooner rather than later.
